text:
COMPLIANCE:
Scene ID: SC_001_007
Allowed events: Artie and Fizz land in the Tutorial Forest. They encounter a basic slime. Artie panics about his 1 HP. Artie attacks the slime. Artie lands a massive critical hit that vaporizes the slime. A loot drop is revealed.
Forbidden milestones: Acquiring the cursed Participation Trophy (happens in 1:8).

Current arm-side / inventory facts: Leather Wallet (stowed, pocket_right), Employee ID Badge (equipped, neck_lanyard).

Durable changes committed: Added XP resource to Artie's continuity system state. Added milestone for surviving the first encounter.

APPEARANCE_CHECK:
- CHAR_ARTIE: messy brown hair, muddy brown eyes, pale skin, skinny fat build.
- CHAR_FIZZ: neon pink hair, digital blue eyes, translucent skin, tiny ethereal build.

PROSE:
Artie and Fizz landed in the Tutorial Forest, the digital light of their spawn fading into the dappled, pixelated sunlight of the canopy above. Before Artie could even process the smell of artificial pine or the distinctly jagged edges of the surrounding foliage, they were immediately confronted by a basic enemy.

For a first encounter, it wasn't exactly an intimidation masterclass.

A translucent blue slime, roughly the size of a prize-winning pumpkin, sat in the middle of the dirt path. It jiggled. A generic, wet squelching audio file played on a two-second loop, sounding suspiciously like someone stirring a pot of thick macaroni.

"Welcome to the Tutorial Forest!" Fizz announced, her glowing neon pink hair flaring brightly against her translucent skin as she did a little loop-de-loop in the air. "This is your safe zone to learn the basics of movement, inventory management, and, most importantly, combat! Please engage the aggressive fauna to proceed."

Artie ran a trembling hand through his messy brown hair, his muddy brown eyes locked onto the gelatinous blob. His pale, skinny-fat frame was rigid with tension. The slime did not look aggressive. It looked like a dropped gelatin mold. But a small, floating red chevron had appeared above its mass, pulsing with a slow, rhythmic menace.

He had spent his entire adult life avoiding physical confrontation. His idea of a high-stakes encounter was arguing with Karen in HR about expense reports. Now, he was standing in a digital forest, wearing a suit that smelled faintly of ozone and vending machine dust, staring down a hostile dessert.

`[Target: Basic Slime (Lvl. 1)]`
`[HP: 10/10]`

Artie swallowed hard. His throat felt dry. He looked down at his own hands, then mentally summoned his status screen. He didn't need to, he already knew what it said, but the masochistic part of his brain demanded visual confirmation.

`[Artie – Lvl. 1]`
`[HP: 1/1 | Stamina: 10/10]`
`[Critical Hit Rate: 100%]`

"Fizz," Artie whispered, not daring to take his eyes off the jiggling blue blob. "That thing is going to kill me."

"Don't be silly," the tiny, ethereal fairy scoffed, drifting down to hover near his right shoulder. Her digital blue eyes rolled in exaggerated exasperation. "It's a Level 1 Basic Slime. It is literally the weakest entity in the entire RNG-Hellscape compendium. Its base attack deals a maximum of one point of bludgeoning damage. It is mathematically impossible for it to pose a lethal threat to a starting player."

Artie slowly turned his head to look at her. "Fizz. Look at my HP."

Fizz blinked. She pulled up a tiny, holographic clipboard and adjusted a pair of non-existent glasses. "Oh. Right. The Anomaly Integrity Breach. You have exactly one hit point." She tapped her chin thoughtfully. "Well, in that case, yes. It is going to kill you. If it touches you, you will instantly die."

"Are there respawns?!" Artie hissed, his panic spiking.

"Technically, you're already dead," Fizz reminded him cheerfully. "Your current status is 'Dead' due to the vending machine incident. If you die in the system while already dead... well, I'm not entirely sure! Best case scenario, your soul is fragmented and scattered across the void. Worst case scenario, you get rebooted as an NPC in the sanitation department of Oakhaven."

"Sanitation?"

"They deal with the dire-rats. It's a very high-turnover position."

The slime, apparently tired of waiting for Artie to make the first move, initiated its attack sequence. It didn't leap or lunge. Instead, a bright red, glowing rectangle materialized on the dirt path, stretching from the slime's base directly to Artie's cheap leather loafers.

`[Warning: Incoming Attack]`

"Oh god," Artie yelped. He scrambled backward, his dress shoes slipping on the low-resolution mud. He threw himself to the left just as the slime slid forward along the red rectangle, moving at the terrifying speed of a brisk walk.

It missed him by a solid two feet.

Artie hit the ground, his shoulder slamming into a root that felt entirely too polygonal. He scrambled to his feet, his heart hammering against his ribs. He was breathing heavily, sweat beading on his forehead. "It's fast! It's too fast!"

"Artie, its movement speed is coded at zero-point-five meters per second," Fizz said, sounding profoundly unimpressed. "You could literally outwalk it. Just hit it with your primary attack."

"I don't have a weapon!" Artie patted himself down frantically. His right hand brushed his pocket. The familiar, rectangular bulge of his Leather Wallet was still there, safely stowed in his right pocket. The cheap nylon lanyard swung around his neck, the plastic Employee ID Badge smacking him in the chin.

"I have a Leather Wallet and a piece of plastic that says I work in accounts receivable!" Artie shouted, backing away as the slime slowly pivoted to face him again. "Unless this thing accepts Discover card, I am unarmed!"

"You don't need a weapon for a tutorial slime, you big baby," Fizz sighed, crossing her tiny arms. "Just punch it. Or kick it. Or step on it. It only has ten HP. A standard unarmed strike from a human adult does one to two damage. Just kite it and punch it five to ten times."

"If I get within punching distance, it might touch me!" Artie argued. "If it touches me, I go to dire-rat sanitation!"

The slime squelched. The red rectangle appeared on the ground again, this time pointing directly at Artie's new position.

"Wait! Can we talk about this?" Artie yelled at the advancing blob. "I'm not even supposed to be here! I'm an accountant! I have a 401k!"

The slime did not care about his retirement plan. It squelched menacingly, inching forward with the relentless determination of an audit.

Artie backpedaled, keeping his eyes glued to the glowing danger zone. He needed a strategy. He dealt with numbers, risk assessment, and minimizing liabilities. Right now, his liability was a one hundred percent chance of death upon receiving damage, and his asset was a one hundred percent chance of landing a critical hit.

"Fizz," Artie said, his breathing shallow. "What exactly does my critical hit stat do?"

"A critical hit is a localized strike that bypasses standard defense calculations, usually targeting a weak point," Fizz recited, reading from a floating tooltip. "In this system, a standard critical hit applies a times-two multiplier to base damage. However..." She paused, her digital eyes widening slightly. "Your stat isn't just high. It's broken. The system compensated for your zero-point-one Vitality by hard-locking your Crit Rate to maximum, but it didn't cap the multiplier."

"English, Fizz!" Artie yelled, diving behind a nearby tree trunk as the slime slowly slid past him, missing him by a mile.

"It means your critical hits don't just do double damage," Fizz explained, floating through the tree trunk to join him. "Because your Crit Rate is an anomaly, the multiplier scales with the absurdity of the stat imbalance. I don't actually know how much damage you'll do. The math is... weird."

"Weird how?"

"Like, divide-by-zero weird."

The slime hit the tree trunk. It didn't do any damage to the tree, but it did make a wet smack sound, and it began to slowly turn around to face Artie again.

Artie looked at his leather loafer. It was scuffed, cheap, and offered absolutely zero arch support. But it was the only weapon he had.

"Okay," Artie muttered, psyching himself up. "Okay. It's just a gelatin mold. It's a jello shot that wants to murder me. I can do this."

He stepped out from behind the tree.

The slime immediately targeted him. The red rectangle flared on the ground.

Artie didn't run this time. He stood his ground, watching the slime slide toward him. The two-second audio loop of stirring macaroni seemed to grow louder, mocking him. He waited until the slime was halfway down the red path.

He pulled his right leg back. He didn't know martial arts. He didn't know how to fight. But he knew how to kick a jammed copier drawer when it refused to release his tax forms.

"For accounting," Artie whispered.

He swung his leg forward in a brutal, uncoordinated punt, aiming directly for the center of the jiggling blue mass. His loafer sank into the gelatinous surface. For a fraction of a second, Artie felt a terrifying, icy resistance, and he was absolutely certain the slime was going to absorb his foot, deal one point of damage, and end his miserable existence.

Then, the system math caught up with reality.

`[Critical Hit!]`

The impact didn't sound like a kick. It sounded like a tactical orbital strike.

A deafening shockwave echoed through the Tutorial Forest. A blast of pure, distorted kinetic energy erupted from the point of contact. The air itself seemed to shatter, pixelating into jagged shards of light before snapping back into place.

Artie was thrown backward by the sheer force of his own kick, tumbling head over heels through the dirt and crashing into a bush.

`[Damage: 99,999]`

The number floated into the sky, massive and glowing in an angry, jagged red font. It was so large it clipped through the canopy of the trees.

Artie groaned, spitting out a mouthful of low-poly leaves. He checked his UI frantically.

`[Artie – HP: 1/1]`

He was alive. He hadn't taken damage.

He looked back at the path.

The slime was obliterated. It hadn't just died; it had been unmade. The sheer mathematical impossibility of a ninety-nine-thousand damage kick against a ten-HP basic enemy had caused the system to completely delete the creature's physical asset from the environment.

Where the slime had been, there was now a small, smoking crater in the dirt path.

`[Target Defeated.]`
`[Experience Gained: 5 XP]`

Fizz floated down next to Artie, her jaw hanging open in a very un-AI-like expression of shock. She looked at the crater, then looked at Artie's cheap leather shoe.

"Well," Fizz said softly. "That was... certainly a critical hit."

Artie let out a long, shaky breath, his adrenaline crashing hard. He laid his head back against the dirt, staring up at the pixelated sky. "I killed it."

"You didn't just kill it, Artie," Fizz corrected, flying over to inspect the crater. "You vaporized it. The physics engine literally couldn't handle the damage output. It just deleted the mesh."

Artie pushed himself up onto his elbows. "Did I level up?"

"From a Level 1 slime? No. You need a hundred XP to reach Level 2. You got five."

"Five?" Artie complained, rubbing his lower back. "I nearly died of a heart attack and I got five XP?"

"Welcome to the grind," Fizz chirped, her usual cheerful demeanor returning. She pointed down into the smoking crater. "Look on the bright side! The slime is obliterated, leaving behind a loot drop."

Artie dragged himself to his feet, dusting off his suit pants. He walked over to the edge of the crater. Hovering neatly in the center of the scorched earth, spinning slowly on an invisible axis, was a small, glowing object. It cast a faint, golden light against the blackened dirt.

Artie stared at the spinning reward, his heart still hammering against his ribs. He had survived his first fight. He was a one-hit-point wonder, a walking glass cannon in a cheap suit, but he had survived.

Now, all he had to do was claim his prize.
